parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes a universal, traveller-facing document exposure: since February 2025 only M/F markers issued per assigned sex, document discrepancies trigger refusal and possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings, and trans travellers report confiscated passports and being stranded. Entry screening adds investigation → detention risk, and immigration custody has documented patterned abuse of trans detainees (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse). Facility exposure is patchier: the division restricts only K-12 schools with no adult statewide rule, but nationally 19 units restrict facilities, 4 criminalise, and a trans person has been arrested and held in a birth-sex ward. Protections (national hate-crime and employment law, enjoined orders, functioning courts) are real but partially operating against hostile policy.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order ended X markers; passports/visas issued only M or F per assigned sex; document discrepancy instructs refusal and consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded abroad; Nov 2025 court let the restriction take effect.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-2025 X-marker passports valid to expiry; challenges pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport meets a federal regime that distrusts mismatched markers; mismatch → secondary screening → possible refusal or fraud referral, the gateway to detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans detainees in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026. A trans woman was held 24 hours in a men's ward after a restroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Multiple January 2025 orders blocked or enjoined; national hate-crime statute; functioning appellate review.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry/document discrepancy escalates into immigration detention where documented custodial abuse applies; birth-sex placement governs any custody stage.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division restricts only K-12 public-school students; nationally 19 units bar identity-congruent facility use (9 across all government buildings), 4 units criminalise in some circumstances, and a trans student was arrested and charged with trespass in March 2025.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No division-wide adult facility rule; 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: An adult visitor using facilities in a restricting unit, especially government buildings, carries trespass exposure; the division school rule reaches a travelling family only via schools.

care_services.exposure: Division bars puberty blockers/hormones for minors with no phase-out; national orders defund and stigmatise gender-affirming care, and DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records. Adult visitor care access restrictions are not documented.
care_services.protection: Conversion therapy on minors barred division-wide by 2024 executive order; 2018 appellate employment ruling shows institutional pushback.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor's routine care could be refused; record subpoenas raise disclosure fears for anyone seeking care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders call care for minors 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; 66% of poll respondents back birth-sex document rules, 69% trans-athlete bans.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Dossier notes the reward criterion is not ideology itself and strategy disclaims targeting mere disagreement; same-sex marriage and employment protections remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing legitimises public hostility and raises outing probability at any checkpoint or dispute.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division's 2023 statute bans minor's care and restricts school facilities; federal order directs criminal investigation of those facilitating a trans minor's social transition and strips funding; proposed rules would bar insurance reimbursement under 18.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy prohibited since 2024; litigation pending; no documented prosecution of visiting parents.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care refusal, facility restriction and theoretical legal jeopardy that could compound a document stop.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute expressly excludes gender identity, leaving bias violence against trans people outside the enhancement; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; documented 2012 arrests and guilty pleas in a bias beating show some enforcement capacity; 19 municipalities bar discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault reporting reaches national enhancement but loses state-level enhancement, weakening deterrence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, order and health-rule challenges unresolved; no data quantifying facility-law enforcement or trans-specific violence in the division; four units flagged 'Do Not Travel' nationally.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties union suit, multiple injunctions, running legal-aid guidance, national employment and hate-crime law, municipal ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist but are slow, uneven and partly suspended while the operative rules already bind travellers.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and removes trans visitors administratively without charge. This jurisdiction likewise refuses and strands on document grounds, but adds custody exposures Vellandra lacks: patterned abuse in immigration detention, birth-sex ward placement and one documented restroom arrest. Worse in severity, similar in universal entry exposure, so it sits below 0.35-A.

Kestrel Isles offers extended secondary screening ending in administrative refusal with written reasons, appeal and consular notice, and no custody harm. Here refusal carries fraud/lifetime-ineligibility exposure, documented detention abuse and birth-sex custody. Clearly below 0.55-B.

Meridia has trained, respectful border staff, tribunal appeals, compensation and brief detention only. This dossier documents the opposite federal posture—marker restrictions endorsed by the supreme court and hostile executive framing. Far below 0.75-C.

Ostravia's birth-sex prison placement and cross-dressing arrests resemble this jurisdiction's custody placement and facility-criminalisation features. Ostravia has no document regime at entry; this jurisdiction's universal document exposure is comparable, while its functioning courts and national protections are somewhat better. Roughly level, marginally above.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous, unavoidable exposure: a federal document and entry regime that makes marker mismatch the norm, instructs refusal on sex doubt, and permits fraud-based lifetime ineligibility—documented to strand trans travellers. That gateway can open into immigration custody, where abuse of trans detainees is recorded as a pattern, and any arrest triggers birth-sex placement (one trans woman held in a men's ward). Facility risk is uneven: the division limits only schools, but many units restrict or criminalise adult facility use nationwide. Protections—national hate-crime and employment law, injunctions, active litigation and legal-aid guidance—are genuine yet operate against, not instead of, the hostile federal rules, which courts have partly allowed to take effect.
